pinterest.title: Is Marriage in Italy Recognised in Australia? What Australian Couples Need to Know
pinterest.description: Is marriage in Italy recognised in Australia? In most cases, yes. Smartraveller and the Attorney-General's Department say an overseas marriage is generally recognised if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law. You cannot register it here, so bring home the comune's marriage certificate with a Prefettura apostille and a full translation. Our guide covers proof, surnames and celebrating again at home.

pinterest.title: Italian Marriage Certificate in Australia: Apostille, Translation and Proof
pinterest.description: Married in Italy? An Italian marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of marriage in Australia. Before you fly home, ask the comune for its certificate (not the parish's) and book the Prefettura for an apostille; the Australian Embassy in Rome warns appointments are hard to get from May to September. Then have it translated in full by an accredited translator. NAATI can help you find one.

pinterest.title: Change Your Name After Marrying Overseas in Italy: The Australian Rules
pinterest.description: Changing your name after marrying overseas is a separate step from recognition. If you were born in Australia, the Passport Office always needs a name change certificate from an Australian registry. In NSW and Victoria you apply for a change of name, and in Queensland you may not be able to take your partner's name automatically. Book the honeymoon in the names on your current passports.

slides: Married in Italy, or planning to? Here is whether your marriage counts back in Australia.
In most cases, yes. It must be valid under Italian law and would have been valid under Australian law had it taken place here.
You cannot register an Italian marriage in Australia. Ask the comune (town hall) for its marriage certificate, not the parish's.
Book the Prefettura for an apostille before you fly home. The Australian Embassy in Rome warns appointments are hard to get from May to September.
Have the certificate translated in full by an accredited translator. NAATI can help you find one in Australia.
Born in Australia and taking your partner's surname? The Passport Office always needs an Australian name change certificate. Book the honeymoon in your current names.
A party at home? You cannot marry each other again here, but a confirmation of vows or recommitment ceremony is open to you.
Not sure whether to marry at the comune or at home first? Speak with a Wedded Advisor. Nothing is too early or too vague.
instagram_carousel.caption:
Is marriage in Italy recognised in Australia? In most cases, yes, with no form to lodge when you land. The harder questions start once you are home.

You cannot register an Italian marriage here, the certificate is in Italian, and a surname change is a separate application in several states. So the paperwork belongs in the wedding plan, not the honeymoon: the comune's certificate, a Prefettura apostille in the first working days after the ceremony, and a full translation by an accredited translator.

Taking your partner's surname? If you were born in Australia, the Passport Office always needs an Australian name change certificate.

Some couples sidestep most of this by marrying legally in Australia first and keeping the Italian day for the vows, the dinner and the people.

Our full guide covers the legal test, proof, surnames state by state and celebrating again at home. Link in bio.

Which route are you weighing up? Tell us below, or speak with a Wedded Advisor before you put down a venue deposit.
